dissents.topic: Severity of the default change from EXTERNAL to FIXED for turn_detection_mode

positions.position: P0 — silently breaks LSP contract for existing callers; postcondition-weakening change with no deprecation path
P0 — silently breaking for existing users; classic 'tested-not-proved' fallacy with no migration note
P1 — breaking default change that needs to be called out explicitly and split into its own commit
P1 — silent behavior swap; values/time confusion; should be labeled 'changed' not 'fixed' and default should be None with explicit resolution
P1 — silent default flip is cleverness that doesn't earn its keep; either keep EXTERNAL or make the parameter required
Not flagged as a standalone severity item; treated implicitly as part of the invariant-statement issue

dissents.topic: Whether EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED actually exists in the dependency

positions.position: P0 — unproven precondition; if EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED is not defined in the imported speechmatics package, this raises AttributeError at construction; REFUSED until proved
Did not flag — treated the member as existing and focused on the duplication/invariant between the two enums rather than its existence

dissents.topic: How to interpret split_sentences: Optional[bool] with 'or False' coercion

positions.position: P1 — 'or False' coerces None to a meaningful False, value/identity confusion; three names for one fact
P1 — tri-state collapses to bi-state, losing the 'use library default' meaning that other Optional[bool] fields preserve
P2 — silently coerced and double-written through generic loop and explicit assignment; pick one channel
P2 — unconditional overwrite clobbers any non-default SpeechSegmentConfig
P2 — if no meaningful third state, just type it bool=False; Optional buys nothing
P1 — three-valued logic without justification; postcondition unspecified

dissents.topic: Frame-listener narrowing from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame

positions.position: P1 — may silently drop finalization in non-VAD pipelines (push-to-talk, scripted tests); state intent or handle both
P1 — precondition strengthening of handler's effective contract; must be stated in docstring
P1 — behavioral narrowing whose correctness depends on unstated class-hierarchy assumption
P1 — invariant connecting frame types not stated; postcondition ambiguous; also a smuggled-goto pattern in the branch
P2 — warning on a frame the service explicitly subscribed to is noisy and not actionable; essential question (who owns endpointing) should be decided in one place
P2 — warning branch is unreachable in practice; data structure should do the work the conditional pretends to do

issues.description: EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED is referenced but never proved to exist in the dependency
issues.detail: self._enable_vad tests membership against [EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED, EndOfUtteranceMode.EXTERNAL], but only TurnDetectionMode.FIXED is added in the diff. If EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED does not exist in the imported speechmatics package at version 0.0.99+, this raises AttributeError at construction time. No guard for older versions; the dependency contract is unstated.

issues.description: Default change from TurnDetectionMode.EXTERNAL to FIXED silently breaks existing callers
issues.detail: Flipping the default changes runtime semantics for every existing caller who relied on the documented default. The previous default finalized on UserStoppedSpeakingFrame (Pipecat-controlled endpointing); the new default finalizes only on VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame. No deprecation path, no warning, no migration note. Liskov and Dijkstra rate P0; Torvalds, Hickey, and Pike rate P1 — see dissents.

issues.description: TurnDetectionMode and EndOfUtteranceMode are two parallel enums encoding the same concept
issues.detail: Both enums now have FIXED and EXTERNAL members; _enable_vad is derived from end_of_utterance_mode while the user-facing knob and changelog speak in terms of turn_detection_mode. The mapping is implicit, lives elsewhere, and the invariant relating the two enums is never stated. Unify into a single source of truth, or document the relationship as an explicit invariant/mapping function.

issues.description: Frame-listener narrowed from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame without stated contract
issues.detail: process_frame previously finalized on UserStoppedSpeakingFrame and now finalizes only on VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame. If the new type is not a subclass, any pipeline emitting plain UserStoppedSpeakingFrame (manual/programmatic stops, push-to-talk, scripted tests) will silently stop finalizing transcripts. The class-hierarchy assumption and the intended invariant are not documented; no test covers both frame types.

issues.description: split_sentences is an Optional[bool] tri-state collapsed to bi-state via 'or False'
issues.detail: params.split_sentences is typed bool | None (default None) and then passed as 'params.split_sentences or False' when constructing SpeechSegmentConfig. This destroys any 'use library default' interpretation that other Optional[bool] fields in the same params block preserve via the setattr loop. Postcondition is unspecified: either type it bool=False, or preserve the None-means-defer semantics. Knuth, Torvalds, and Pike rate this P2; Hickey, Liskov, and Dijkstra rate it P1.

issues.description: SpeechSegmentConfig is unconditionally constructed and overwrites whatever was set
issues.detail: config.speech_segment_config = SpeechSegmentConfig(emit_sentences=params.split_sentences or False) runs every time, clobbering any non-default SpeechSegmentConfig the SDK or earlier branch might have produced. split_sentences is also passed through the generic copy loop AND explicitly assigned — pick one channel. The current double-write makes it unclear which write wins.

issues.description: _enable_vad invariant is unstated and the variable name no longer reflects what it computes
issues.detail: _enable_vad now means 'VAD is on AND user did not pick a Pipecat-controlled mode (FIXED/EXTERNAL)', but the name reads as 'VAD is on'. The invariant linking turn_detection_mode (user-facing) to end_of_utterance_mode (gate) is never stated in code. Either rename (e.g., _emit_vad_frames), derive directly from turn_detection_mode, or document the invariant inline.

issues.description: PR bundles three independent changes: new feature (split_sentences), default change (FIXED), and frame-listener fix
issues.detail: Each should land as its own commit so each can be reverted independently when something downstream breaks. As submitted, a bisect that lands on this commit cannot distinguish which sub-change caused a regression. Torvalds calls this THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: process_frame branch is a smuggled-goto: boolean and its negation as sibling branches with hidden precondition
issues.detail: The structure 'if self._enable_vad: warn; elif not self._enable_vad and self._client is not None: finalize' uses a negated flag and a 'client is not None' rider to encode a precondition that should be stated explicitly at function entry. Refactor to: early-return on enable_vad, then assert/guard client, then finalize. The current form forces the reader to simulate execution.

issues.description: Commented-out start_processing_metrics() call relocated rather than deleted or activated
issues.detail: The line '# await self.start_processing_metrics()' was moved from after the broadcast/interruption calls to before them, still commented. Either the metric belongs at a specific point (uncomment with rationale) or it does not (delete). Moving dead code carries an implicit ordering claim and is noise that future readers will treat as intentional.

issues.description: _prepare_config uses a hand-maintained string list + getattr/setattr/hasattr loop
issues.detail: An allowlist of attribute names with hasattr/setattr loses static checkability, hides which fields the SDK actually supports, and now redundantly includes 'split_sentences' which is also set explicitly via SpeechSegmentConfig. A dataclass-driven iteration or explicit assignments would make value flow obvious and version drift easier to spot. The current shape guarantees the next contributor will forget an entry.

issues.description: Warning branch on VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame when _enable_vad is True is noisy and effectively unreachable
issues.detail: If internal VAD is being used, the upstream pipeline shouldn't be sending this frame; if it does, a per-frame warning is noisy and not actionable. The essential question — who owns endpointing — should be decided in one place, not re-litigated on every frame. Pike notes the dead branch is a signal that the data structure should be doing the work the conditional pretends to do.

issues.description: List-membership check builds a fresh list per evaluation; could be a tuple/frozenset
issues.detail: 'not in [EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED, EndOfUtteranceMode.EXTERNAL]' constructs a fresh list each time; a tuple is idiomatic and cheaper. Minor performance/style nit but fits the broader 'use one source of truth' concern.

issues.description: Changelog files disagree on whether FIXED is added or fixed; PR description omits split_sentences
issues.detail: changelog/3328.added.md mentions only split_sentences; changelog/3328.fixed.md covers VAD frame change, default change, and conditional emission. The new FIXED enum value is arguably 'added,' not 'fixed.' Separately, the PR description enumerates three changes and never mentions split_sentences, even though the diff adds the parameter, an InputParams field, config wiring, and a changelog entry — reviewer cannot reconcile stated scope with delivered scope.

issues.description: No tests in the diff for default-behavior change, new parameter, or frame-listener swap
issues.detail: The patch changes default behavior, adds a parameter, and swaps a frame listener with zero test changes. The commit message should at minimum describe how the change was validated against a live Speechmatics endpoint; otherwise the review takes 'it works' on faith.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on two contract-level problems and one structural smell. First, the default flip from TurnDetectionMode.EXTERNAL to FIXED is a silently breaking change for every existing caller — five of six reviewers flag it, with Liskov and Dijkstra calling it P0 (postcondition weakened with no deprecation) while Torvalds, Hickey, and Pike rate it P1 (breaking default that needs to be labeled and migrated, not buried in a 'fixed' changelog entry). Second, the new TurnDetectionMode.FIXED parallels an existing EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED, and _enable_vad is gated on the latter while users configure the former — four reviewers (Knuth, Hickey, Liskov, Pike) call out this complecting/invariant gap. The narrowed frame listener (UserStoppedSpeakingFrame → VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame) is flagged by four reviewers as a contract change whose class-hierarchy assumption and effect on non-VAD pipelines is undocumented. The strongest preserved disagreement is Dijkstra's P0-only claim that EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED may not exist in the dependency at all — a precondition no other reviewer addressed; if true, this raises AttributeError at construction and warrants REFUSED status independent of every other issue.
